title: Requirements and verification
statement: Systems engineering distinguishes a requirement, which states a needed outcome or constraint, from verification evidence showing that the implemented system satisfies the declared requirement.
limitations: Verification against a flawed requirement does not establish that the resulting system is useful, safe, or fit for its real context.

title: Feedback control loop
statement: A feedback controller compares measured system behavior with a target or reference and uses the difference to adjust inputs according to a declared control law.
limitations: Feedback can stabilize or destabilize a system depending on dynamics, delay, sensing, actuator limits, and controller design.

title: Engineering margin
statement: Engineering margin separates a predicted operating demand from a declared limit so uncertainty, variation, degradation, and model error can be considered in design decisions.
limitations: A margin is meaningful only with a specified failure mode, units, model, uncertainty basis, and acceptance rule.

title: Correlation does not by itself establish causation
statement: An observed association between variables does not alone identify a causal effect because confounding, selection, measurement error, reverse direction, and chance can produce or distort associations.
limitations: Associations can still be informative when combined with design, assumptions, mechanisms, and converging evidence.

title: Working memory
statement: Working memory refers to limited-capacity processes that temporarily maintain and manipulate information needed for an ongoing cognitive task.
limitations: Working memory is modeled in multiple ways, and capacity estimates depend on task design and strategy.

title: Population rate
statement: A demographic rate relates events occurring during a specified period to the population exposed to the possibility of those events, with a declared denominator and time basis.
limitations: Rates are not directly comparable unless case definitions, population structure, observation windows, and standardization are compatible.

title: Phonetics and phonology
statement: Phonetics studies the physical production, transmission, and perception of speech sounds, while phonology studies how languages organize sound patterns and contrasts within linguistic systems.
limitations: The boundary is analytically useful but the two fields interact closely in real speech and language change.

title: Word-order typology
statement: Language typology compares recurring structural patterns across languages, including relative ordering patterns such as subject, object, and verb, without treating one pattern as universally superior.
limitations: Category assignments can depend on construction, discourse context, and descriptive analysis; languages may show more than one order.

title: Dependency annotation
statement: Dependency annotation represents syntactic structure with directed relations linking words to heads under an explicit annotation scheme, enabling comparable computational analysis when guidelines are applied consistently.
limitations: Treebank licenses differ, annotation decisions are theory-informed, and agreement does not make the annotation scheme the only valid linguistic analysis.
